key_insight: A GPU-accelerated one-way Eulerian-Lagrangian framework can efficiently couple 2D incompressible flow with passive tracers and inertial particles while preserving accurate transport dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The method enables scalable, single-GPU simulation of turbulent particle transport, making it useful for studying dispersion, coherent-structure interactions, and preferential concentration in incompressible flows.
method: Fourier pseudospectral Navier-Stokes solver with second-order Adams-Bashforth time integration
Particle trajectories advanced with fourth-order Runge-Kutta for tracer and inertial dynamics
Fluid-to-particle coupling via bilinear, bicubic Catmull-Rom, or bicubic B-spline interpolation
evidence_signal: Verification against analytical solutions and benchmark tests shows the solver is stable and accurate, and bilinear interpolation gives transport statistics nearly identical to higher-order schemes.
watch_item: The framework is one-way coupled, so particle feedback on the fluid is not modeled and may limit applicability for dense or strongly interacting suspensions.
paper_title: A coupled Eulerian Lagrangian approach for fluid and particle dynamics
